tagline: Up the seaside of the Eastern Shore, between two waters.
intro: Seaside Road leaves US 13 at Kiptopeke, near the bottom of the Eastern Shore, and runs north up the peninsula past Eastville, the county seat, to Nassawadox. The town's name means land between two waters, with the Atlantic to the east and the Chesapeake to the west. Farther north the byway crosses the peninsula on SR 180, from the village of Pungoteague to the waterfront at Wachapreague, then goes on through Accomac to Onancock.

Onancock was in at the very end of the Revolution. In November 1782, 25 of its men joined Commodore Zedechiah Whaley against British barges in the bay, and he surrendered on the day the peace treaty was drafted.

moments.title: Kiptopeke State Park
moments.text: At the old landing of the ferry across the bay, retired in 1964 when the Bridge-Tunnel opened, concrete ships were sunk to hold off storm erosion.

moments.title: Wachapreague
moments.text: SR 180 ends on the waterfront, where the Wachapreague Channel winds out through the seaside marsh to the barrier islands and reaches the Atlantic between Cedar and Parramore islands.

moments.title: Onancock
moments.text: A town on Onancock Creek founded in 1680, once a stop on the stagecoach line between Wilmington, Delaware and Eastville.
